archetype: Burst-oriented LUK thief built on two separate energy pools rather than a combo counter. Attribute attacks come in three flavours (Heaven, Earth, Humanity); cycling through all three advances an Attribute Combo that feeds Talisman Energy, and Talisman skills in turn feed Scroll Energy. Talisman and Scroll skills spend those pools. The class doc describes it as a three-minute burst class whose selling point is its movement and utility kit (a free-flight skill, a placed warp gate, a variable-duration iframe, a short on-demand Dark Sight) rather than raw single-target damage.

linkSkill.name: Bravado

linkSkill.levels: Master Level 3. Lv.1: Ignore Defense +5%, damage vs 100%-HP enemies +9%. Lv.2: Ignore Defense +10%, damage vs 100%-HP enemies +14%. Lv.3: Ignore Defense +15%, Damage +4%, damage vs 100%-HP enemies +19%.

legionEffect: Flat LUK: +10 / +20 / +40 / +80 / +100 across Legion ranks B through SSS.

priority.node: SYSTEM CHANGE FIRST - as of GMS v269 there are no craftable boost node trios. Every job is handed a fixed set of nodes and Nodestones now grant V Points used to level them. Hoyoung's fixed set is six boost nodes and four job nodes.
priority.why: This is the single biggest trap for anyone reading older Hoyoung material: guides written before 17 June 2026 tell you which three skills to pair in a trio, and that decision no longer exists. The only remaining decision is which of the six given boost nodes to spend V Points on.
priority.verifiedClaim: maplestorywiki.net's V Matrix Update History entry reads, verbatim: 'update GMS 269 June 17 2026 (Ride the Lightning): The V Matrix received an overhaul. Nodestones now grant V Points to upgrade Nodes. Each job receives a fixed amount of Nodes to upgrade.' The same page's body reads 'Each player will receive 4 job nodes' and 'Each player will receive 6 boost nodes, with each one enhancing between 1 and 4 individual skills.' Grandis Library and NamuWiki each list exactly six fixed Hoyoung boost node groupings rather than a trio-crafting scheme, which corroborates the outcome.
priority.consensusNote: Three independent sources, but only maplestorywiki carries the dated patch entry itself; Grandis and NamuWiki corroborate the outcome (six fixed nodes) rather than the patch statement. Deliberately not labelled strong for that reason.

priority.node: Spend on boost nodes 1-4 (the four that feed a 6th job HEXA Mastery) before nodes 5-6.
priority.why: Nodes 1-4 are exactly the four whose skill sets match the four HEXA Mastery cores, so points spent there keep paying out after 260; nodes 5-6 have no Mastery attached.
priority.verifiedClaim: Three checks, all re-run 2026-09-12. (a) Mechanical criterion: maplestorywiki's V Matrix page states boost nodes have 'maximum Level is 60, and they must be Level 40 to unlock their corresponding HEXA Mastery Nodes.' (b) Contents match: maplestorywiki's Hoyoung Mastery Node/Core 1-4 contain exactly the skills in Boost Node/Enhancement Core 1-4, skill for skill. (c) Tiering: Grandis Library's page data marks nodes 1-4 PRIMARY and nodes 5-6 SECONDARY, with the legend 'PRIMARY: Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used' / 'SECONDARY: Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used'. NamuWiki independently splits the same six groupings into 필수 강화 코어 (essential, the same four) and 선택 강화 코어 (optional, the same two).
priority.consensusNote: Three independent lanes: maplestorywiki (two pages, counted once), Grandis Library, NamuWiki. Grandis credits its Boost Nodes Build field to the class doc, so Grandis and the class doc are one lineage - but NamuWiki's essential/optional split is genuinely outside that lineage and lands on the same 4/2 division.

priority.node: Overall V Matrix spend order stated by the class doc, verbatim: 'Boosts > Decent Holy Symbol > Clone Rampage > Wrath of Gods > Apparition >= Tiger > Last Resort > Grandis Blessing > Other Decents > Will of Erda > Other'.
priority.why: Boost nodes come first because they scale every use of the skills underneath them and gate the HEXA Masteries; the four job skills are then ranked by how much of Hoyoung's burst each one actually contributes.
priority.verifiedClaim: The order string above was read verbatim off the class doc's V Matrix page on 2026-09-12, together with its own caveat: 'This order is just a general recommendation, feel free to upgrade based on personal preference and play style.' NamuWiki independently states the same job-node ranking: '직업 코어는 선기 : 극대 분신난무 > 선기 : 강림 괴력난신 ≥ 선기 : 천지인 환영 > 권술 : 산령소환 순으로 강화한다' - Clone Rampage, then Wrath of Gods, then Three Paths Apparition, then Tiger of Songyu, with the reason that Clone Rampage's utility is greatest and Tiger of Songyu is the smallest share of 5th job damage. The two sources place the tie marker differently (the doc writes Apparition >= Tiger, NamuWiki writes Wrath of Gods >= Apparition); the sequence is identical.
priority.consensusNote: Downgraded from the previous 'strong' label: two independent lineages is moderate under the 3+ rule, not strong. Both sources publish it as a recommendation, and the class doc explicitly disclaims it as a rule.

vMatrix.notes: Mechanics re-read off maplestorywiki.net/w/V_Matrix on 2026-09-12. At Lv.200 you open the V Matrix with 12 node slots (raised from 7 by GMS v255, 2024-11-20) and the maximum is 30. Matrix points: 1 per level from 200-220, then 2 per level from 221-260, after which point gain stops; an additional node slot opens at Lv. 210, 220, 230, 240, 250 and 260. Boost nodes cap at Lv.60 and 'must be Level 40 to unlock their corresponding HEXA Mastery Nodes'. Job nodes cap at Lv.30 and 'must be Level 25 to unlock their corresponding HEXA Boost Nodes' - note that this is the V Matrix page's wording, while the Hoyoung skill page's HEXA Enhancements section says instead that Enhancements 'require the corresponding V Skill to be leveled to max and equipped'. The same wiki is internally inconsistent about whether the job-node gate is 25 or 30; both statements are recorded rather than picking one. Practical bridge for this class: the four PRIMARY boost nodes need 40 and the four job skills need at least 25 before Hoyoung's HEXA Mastery or Enhancement cores can be touched. Separately, the class doc's V Matrix page still shows the pre-v269 trio images and has not been rewritten for the overhaul, so read its Node Upgrade Order line and ignore its trio tables.

order.step: Mastery Core 1 - the Consuming Flames / Stone Tremor / Gold-Banded Cudgel core carrying the Universal Harmony buff - is the first HEXA core to invest in.
order.why: The payoff is not only the upgraded Heaven/Earth/Humanity attacks but the Universal Harmony buff they trigger, whose effect grows by 1 percentage point every 6 levels - so the core carries more value per level than the other 6th job cores.
order.verifiedClaim: NamuWiki states, verbatim: '강화된 천지인 스킬의 피해량 자체도 강력하지만, 그보다도 최종 데미지 증가로 인한 전반적인 피해량 증가폭이 크다. 특히 버프 효과가 6레벨당 1%p씩 증가하므로, 호영은 멸화염/지진쇄/금고봉 마스터리 코어의 강화를 다른 6차 코어보다 우선해야 한다.' - the enhanced Heaven/Earth/Humanity skills hit hard, but the broader gain from the Final Damage increase is larger, and because the buff effect rises 1%p every 6 levels, Hoyoung should prioritise the Consuming Flames / Stone Tremor / Gold-Banded Cudgel mastery core over the other 6th job cores. maplestorywiki independently confirms Universal Harmony sits inside Mastery Node/Core 1.
order.consensusNote: DOWNGRADED from the previous 'strong - two independent lineages'. The judgement has exactly one publisher, NamuWiki. The second lineage previously claimed was the class doc's HEXA tracker spreadsheet, whose grid could not be read this session and which is in any case derived from MapleScouter and from the class doc family - not an independent vote. maplestorywiki is cited here only to confirm that Universal Harmony really is in Mastery Core 1; it makes no priority judgement. NamuWiki is KMS-balance, so the conclusion may not transfer cleanly to GMS Heroic.

order.step: Sol Janus to level 1 early, unless the character is a pure boss mule that neither trains nor farms.
order.why: The class doc justifies it on time saved rather than on damage. Beyond level 1 it names 10, 20 and 30 as all valid stopping points depending on training map and progression, and notes Hoyoung can already clear most maps with one or two Dawn Orbs or with Dusk Lightning, so the case for pushing Sol Janus further is weaker than for classes that need it to clear.
order.verifiedClaim: Read verbatim off the class doc's Sol Janus page on 2026-09-12: unlocking Sol Janus to level 1 'should be a top priority due to the significant time savings in dailies and farming', 'unless your Hoyoung is just a boss mule that doesn't do either'; 'Depending on your training map and progression, level 10, 20, or 30 are all valid options'; and 'Hoyoung can clear most maps easily with one or two Dawn Orbs (or with Dusk Lightning)'. The previous draft's extra clause 'and on whether the goal is level 290' was DELETED - the page talks about level advantage providing more FD in general terms and names no such target.
order.consensusNote: Single lineage (class doc). No independent source for Sol Janus timing on this class was located.

order.step: Sage: Clone Rampage Boost is the one Enhancement core with a class-specific wrinkle: taking it from 29 to 30 is worse value than starting another core.
order.why: Unlike Hoyoung's other Enhancement cores, its gain per level is flat with no jump at the level-30 breakpoint, while the Sol Erda and fragment cost of that breakpoint is unchanged.
order.verifiedClaim: UPGRADED this pass from weak to moderate because maplestorywiki's own level tables independently demonstrate the claim NamuWiki makes. NamuWiki: '다른 강화 코어와 달리 레벨당 증가량이 일정하다. 단, 10의 단위 레벨마다 요구하는 솔 에르다 및 조각의 요구량에는 변동이 없다. 따라서 29레벨에서 30레벨로 넘어가는 단계라면 다른 코어를 먼저 강화할 것이 권장된다.' Independently, maplestorywiki's HEXA Enhancements section states 'Final Damage bonuses from Enhancements increase linearly each level, with a jump at levels 10, 20, and 30', and its per-level tables show Sage: Clone Rampage Boost going 452 at Lv.1, 548 at 9, 560 at 10, 668 at 19, 680 at 20, 788 at 29, 800 at 30 - a flat +12 per level with no breakpoint jump - while Scroll: Tiger of Songyu Boost goes +49% at 29 to +60% at 30, an eleven-point jump. The numbers confirm the caveat.

order.step: HEXA Stat unlock gates. HEXA Stat I opens at Lv.260; the class doc says to unlock it after raising Rampage to level 5 on Heroic, or 4 on Interactive. HEXA Stat II opens at Lv.265; unlock it once Universal Harmony (Mastery I) reaches Lv.18, on both server types. HEXA Stat III opens at Lv.270; after Apotheosis reaches 5 on Heroic, or Tiger reaches 1 on Interactive.
order.why: These are the doc's own checkpoints for when a HEXA Stat is worth opening relative to skill investment, and they are the one place the doc separates Heroic from Interactive explicitly.
order.verifiedClaim: Read off the class doc's HEXA Stat page on 2026-09-12, matching level-for-level. One correction: the doc writes 'Rampage' and 'Apotheosis' plainly; the previous draft rendered the HEXA Stat I gate as 'Sage: Clone Rampage's Enhancement to 5', which adds a specificity (skill node versus Enhancement core) the page does not state. That specificity was removed.
order.consensusNote: Single lineage (class doc), but stated as plain text rather than encoded in an image.

order.step: HEXA Stat line setup. Opening configuration: main stat to ATT, the two additional stats to Crit Damage and LUK. Keep enhancing until the main stat reaches level 3, where the cost steps from 10 to 20, then decide whether to finish the node now for a small across-the-board gain or park it and focus on specific skills. Once maxed, prioritise ATT above LUK above Crit Damage. For HEXA Stats II and III the doc declines to give a fixed answer and points at MapleScouter instead.
order.why: Recorded as stated because the doc deliberately stops short of a universal answer on the second and third stat nodes - it says to use MapleScouter to check what is best personally.
order.verifiedClaim: Read off the class doc's HEXA Stat page on 2026-09-12: 'MAIN STAT to ATT', 'ADDITIONAL STATS to Crit Damage and LUK', 'Keep Enhancing until MAIN STAT gets to level 3 (cost increase from 10 to 20)', 'Prioritise highest levels/stat for ATT > LUK > Crit Damage' because 'ATT is affected by % lines, LUK is a flat bonus (final stat)', and 'Use MapleScouter to check what is best for you personally' for Stats II and III. One correction: the previous draft said the cost steps 'from 10 to 20 fragments'; the page does not name the unit, so 'fragments' was removed.
order.consensusNote: Single lineage. The doc itself treats HEXA Stats II and III as a per-character computation, which should be surfaced to a user rather than replaced with a static list.

hexa.orderShapeNote: This array is an ordered PRIORITY list only for its first two entries, which are the only genuinely sequenced claims any reachable source makes (Mastery Core 1 first; Sol Janus to 1 early). The remaining entries are gates and configuration advice that apply when their level thresholds arrive, not further steps in a ranking. Downstream code must not read positions 3-5 as 'third, fourth, fifth priority'.
hexa.deletedThisPass: A previously recorded 18-step HEXA sequence ('Universal Harmony to 1, Talisman Mastery to 1, Scroll Mastery to 1, Sol Hecate to 1, Universal Harmony to 6, ...') was DELETED. It was attributed to a live-computed cell in the class doc's tracker spreadsheet; the spreadsheet grid could not be read this session, the value is input-dependent and preset-dependent by the file's own admission, and it used two mastery-core nicknames that appear in no reachable source. An ordered 18-step array that a planner would diff a player's build against is exactly the shape that must not outrun its evidence. Also DELETED: the claim that the four Enhancement cores should be levelled in the order Clone Rampage, Wrath of Gods, Three Paths Apparition, Tiger of Songyu. That ordering is real for the 5TH JOB job nodes (see vMatrix.priority) but neither the class doc nor NamuWiki states it for HEXA Enhancement cores; carrying it over was an inference presented as a citation.
hexa.notes: Deliberately left out rather than guessed: any full step-by-step HEXA order, and any Sol Erda versus Sol Erda Fragment budgeting split. The class doc publishes its Heroic priority only as an infographic, and the doc's own hint above that image reads, verbatim: 'The heroic hexa priority displayed is a simplifed version, which gives similar FD with fewer steps. For full optimization and extra breakpoints, check MapleScouter or the Hoyoung HEXA Matrix Tracker sheet.' That warning is the doc's, re-read 2026-09-12, and is why the image was not transcribed; the page's tracker section self-stamps 'Updated 26/02/2025'. General HEXA mechanic worth knowing: because the Sol Erda and fragment cost of the level-30 step is identical for every core, going 29 to 30 on a core is often worse than starting another core - and for Sage: Clone Rampage Boost specifically it always is, since that core has no level-30 jump.

Ideal Approach: start with Miracle Circulators and roll Boss Damage on either the 2nd or 3rd line; then switch to Honor EXP and roll Abnormal Status Damage on whichever of those two does not already have Boss Damage, AND roll Passive Skills +1 on the 1st line. The doc's stated reason: 'This method is efficient because Abnormal Status Damage has a smaller range variance, making it easier to maximize.' gearingNotes: Four things change Hoyoung's gearing relative to a generic thief. (1) Crit rate is largely self-supplied: Grandis's base-stat table totals +55% critical rate from Hoyoung's own skills, on top of the 5% base. Source: https://grandislibrary.com/anima/hoyoung. (2) Attack speed needs no help from inner ability or gear beyond the usual: the class doc states Hoyoung hits attack speed 0 with its own Booster plus a Decent Speed Infusion node plus a green potion, and says outright that the attack speed +1 inner ability line is not needed. It also notes GMS gains roughly 6-7% final damage from reaching attack speed 0 on a dummy compared to KMS, less in a real fight. Source: https://www.hoyoung.directory/introduction/faq. (3) No cooldown-reduction hat for bossing. The class doc's position is that a CD hat only trims a second or two off Hoyoung's AoE cooldowns, that cooldown-skip inner ability is unreliable, and that Hoyoung already gets natural resets from its V skill - and that the main stat given up on a CD hat costs more across the burst skills than the Gold-Banded Cudgel gain is worth. It allows one exception: a CD hat can be worth it for training if Consuming Flames is wanted in every rotation. Source: https://www.hoyoung.directory/introduction/faq. (4) The Lv.200 storyline is not optional. Completing Sealing the Fiends: The Final Act 2 at Lv.200 grants Fiend Seal, a permanent ATT +10% and Final Damage +10%, plus the Exclusive Spell echo. For a character sitting at Lv.200 this is the single largest free damage source available and it is gated behind quest text, not gear. Source: https://www.hoyoung.directory/introduction/faq. Base stat reference, all from https://grandislibrary.com/anima/hoyoung: weapon multiplier 1.3x, weapon mastery 90%, boss damage +20% and ignore defense roughly +41.7% from skills before the Bravado link skill.

commonMistakes.mistake: Skipping the Hoyoung storyline. Two quests matter: The Missing Trainee 3 at Lv.10 grants Nimbus Cloud, and Sealing the Fiends: The Final Act 2 at Lv.200 grants Fiend Seal, worth ATT +10% and Final Damage +10% permanently.
Not locking Nimbus Cloud after receiving it. The class doc says to lock the skill so that up jump keeps working.

Not locking Universal Harmony once HEXA Mastery core 2 is unlocked. Universal Harmony empowers both the spammable Attribute attacks and the cooldown ones, so once Mastery Node/Core 2 is in play the enhanced charges get eaten by basic attacks unless the buff is right-clicked to lock, leaving them for Stone Tremor or Gold-Banded Cudgel instead. The class doc states this twice, on the skills page and again in its HEXA common questions.
Releasing Sage: Apotheosis early. For full damage the key is held until the full-screen mountains appear.

evidenceNotes: Independence audit, re-run 2026-09-12. Grandis Library's Hoyoung page credits Inner Ability, Hyper Passive Build and Boost Nodes Build to 'Class Doc', so Grandis and hoyoung.directory are ONE source on every judgement field. Grandis's own compiled data - the base-stats-from-skills table and the 6th Job skill list - is not credited to the class doc and is treated as independent for those facts only. The HEXA trackers are by the class doc's own community and their priority presets derive from MapleScouter, so tracker, class doc and MapleScouter are one lineage. That leaves three genuinely independent lanes: (1) the class doc family; (2) NamuWiki's Korean skill page, the only outside judgement source found, KMS-balance; (3) maplestorywiki.net, independent but judgement-free, used for node contents, skill names, effect values, per-level enhancement tables and the dated v269 system change. mastermysty's node table is a fourth independent lane but is obsolete for building. Reachability this pass: hoyoung.directory (all pages, via .md siblings and /llms.txt), grandislibrary.com (page data read directly), maplestorywiki.net (403 to a plain fetch, 200 with a browser user agent) and mystyjl.github.io all responded. en.namu.wiki returned 403; the Korean original at namu.wiki served the same article and was used instead - same document, same source, different host. The class doc's HEXA tracker spreadsheet returned only its page shell with no grid data, so nothing inside it could be verified and every claim resting solely on it was deleted or demoted. Consequence: V Matrix node contents and tiering, the v269 system change, the 5th job job-node order and the Clone Rampage flat-scaling caveat are well corroborated; the Universal Harmony HEXA priority, inner ability, hyper passives, Sol Janus timing and all HEXA Stat guidance rest on a single lineage and are labelled weak accordingly.
